title: Complete clause initialism under one unknown global alphabet key
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED, NOT SELECTED: compile every complete source clause by taking exactly the first written letter of each word, preserving word order, and applying one global injective letter-to-written-symbol map; one complete clause becomes one complete written group. This gives no free sentence or word glosses and predicts new words through initials already learned from other words. Historical support currently reaches formula initialisms in the transmitted Ciceronian correspondence (Perseus commentary: https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus%3Atext%3A1999.04.0076%3Atext%3Dcomm&force=y); a continuous late-medieval technical exemplar, fixed source repertoire, and source-authored clause boundaries are not established. Free plaintext is non-identifiable because distinct complete grammatical sentences can have identical ordered initials; any recovery claim must retain the full preimage within an independently frozen source repertoire. No target or control fit performed.

design.mechanism: For source clause S=(w1,...,wn), compiler C_k(S)=k(first(w1))...k(first(wn)), with one global injective k. Clause separators become group separators; complete historical passages retain all clauses and their order. No dropped words, free macro replacements, character resemblance assumptions, or learned output strings.
design.unit: An entire historical clause or sentence is one complete written group; each written symbol represents a word-initial equivalence class shared across all clauses.
design.contrast: Unlike GDT893, code sharing is forced between every pair of different source words with the same initial. Unlike GDT609/GDT614, no freely assigned stem/syllable or paid macro output exists. This is still a finite-state projection, not a new automata class. Unlike the rejected GDT735 mnemonic, no EVA label is identified with a Latin initial: all global alphabet permutations remain unknown.
design.prediction: A separately fixed complete source continuation whose initials are all covered by the discovery key predicts every glyph and whole-group length, including words absent from discovery. All source aliases and all key solutions must agree before claiming a point prediction. A different group length or a single certain glyph contradiction refutes that fixed compilation. No re-alignment or new source-window selection is allowed.
design.scope: Prospective finite historical source repertoire and exact boundary rule remain unfixed; no manuscript admission or semantic interpretation is granted. Source-only full-preimage identifiability is necessary before implementation.
